title: Four Steps Complex Mapping with Nested Grid
full_prompt: Write a complete ManimGL script using the InteractiveScene class to visualize the four-step conformal mapping process of a Droste-effect spiral. The scene, named FourStepsWithGrid, should set up four complex coordinate planes arranged in a 2x2 grid layout (Planes A, B, C, and D). On Plane A, generate a nested square grid that recursively scales inward to represent infinite detail. Implement a helper function `apply_func_between_planes` to map mobjects from a source plane to a target plane using a given complex function. Step 1: Show the nested grid on Plane A. Step 2: Map this grid to Plane B using the complex logarithm function, transforming concentric squares into parallel vertical/horizontal lines. Step 3: Apply a complex linear transformation (scaling and rotation) to map the grid from Plane B to Plane C, representing the twist in the log-plane. Step 4: Map the grid from Plane C to Plane D using the complex exponential function, showing how the twisted grid wraps back into a seamless spiral Droste grid. Use arrows to indicate the flow between the planes (A -> B, B -> C, C -> D) and include a glowing blank spot at the origin of Plane D to represent the singularity.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Incorrect coordinate mapping between planes due to wrong origin shifts or unit size scaling
common_failure_modes.note: The helper function apply_func_between_planes must precisely shift to origin, scale to unit size, apply the complex function, scale back, and shift to the target plane.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Infinite recursion or memory exhaustion when generating nested square grids
common_failure_modes.note: Limit the recursion depth (n_recursions) to a reasonable number like 5 or 6 to avoid performance degradation.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing texture files or incorrect path resolution for TexturedSurface
common_failure_modes.note: Ensure fallback mechanisms or mock textures are used if external PNG files are not present in the local directory.
